title: organism_sim: open-ended task generation at 12-16 bits with a pre-registered XCS base learner (v0.4.0)
description:
Archival release of organism_sim, an artificial-life simulation of rule-evolving agents (XCS-lineage Learning Classifier System, closed s-expression action DSL from dna::}{::lang 0.2, routed message bus, hash-chained telemetry). Pure NumPy, seeded and deterministic; no hardware, no physical constants, no language model in the execution loop.

This release adds two pre-registered positive results and their data: Substrate-Opt-2, which reduces 16-bit drift recovery from 8,750 to 6,000 trials per shift on 5/5 held-out seeds (population size N=4000 with tournament selection; the judged configuration is frozen as lcs.PARAMS16), and M3b, in which POET-style open-ended task generation reaches pooled ANNECS 35 vs 25 (ratio 1.40, 4/5 seeds) at 12-16 bits - reversing the same machinery's earlier documented FAIL at 6-10 bits.

Two confounds in M3b are reported with the result: a width-coverage artifact in one auxiliary criterion, and the fact that the winning arm bundles curriculum with competence inheritance. The ablation separating them (M3c, fresh seeds 70-74) is pre-registered in docs/PROGRAM.md and was executing at the time of this deposit.

Seven of the eleven pre-registered experiments in this record are negative and are retained in full: offline and LLM-authored priors, specificity-matched priors (three independent samples), evolved regulatory genes (which exhibited specification gaming), concept drift, and a 55-point XCS grid that failed to move the same ceiling Substrate-Opt-2 later moved. Every criterion was committed to git before its run; evaluation seeds are disjoint from tuning seeds; the scorecard in README.md is generated from the files under results/ and guarded by a test.
references: Wang, R., Lehman, J., Clune, J., Stanley, K. O. (2019). Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET).
Brant, J. C., Stanley, K. O. (2017). Minimal criterion coevolution.
Butz, M. V., Sastry, K., Goldberg, D. E. (2003). Tournament selection in XCS.
Lanzi, P. L. (1997). A study of the generalization capabilities of XCS.
Wilson, S. W. (1995). Classifier fitness based on accuracy.
